name: K. Tanaka
bio: Cyberpunk illustrator drawn to the density of Asian megacities. Neon Kowloon reimagines the Walled City as a vertical labyrinth of light — a love letter to a place that no longer exists.

name: Lin Wei
bio: Contemporary ink painter working in the Dunhuang tradition. Lin Wei's line work strips the flying apsara down to pure motion, letting silk carry what the cave walls once held.

name: M. Dubois
bio: French painter examining the Eastern figure through a Western gaze. The Last Emperor is part of The Other Gaze — a collection dedicated to non-Eastern artists redefining Oriental themes.

name: Studio Kaiju
bio: An Osaka-based design collective obsessed with monsters and machines. Dragon Mecha fuses the Chinese dragon with biomechanical engineering — mythology rebuilt as hardware.

name: A. Rivera × LYS
bio: Illustrator A. Rivera in co-creation with the LYS studio. Bruce Lee — The Flow captures movement rather than likeness, a portrait of energy instead of a face.

name: S. Okafor
bio: Lagos-born, Lisbon-based visual artist translating sound into image. Midnight Jazz turns smoky club light and brass curves into pure colour field.

name: Wang Yue
bio: Architectural pattern-maker deconstructing imperial ornament. Palace Geometry reduces Forbidden City motifs to their underlying grid — heritage rendered as pure structure.

name: Chen Hao
bio: Mythology illustrator reworking Chinese deities with graphic weight. Erlang Shen gives the three-eyed god a bold contemporary presence without losing the old power.

name: Yuki Sato
bio: Kyoto ink wash painter working with restraint. Ink Bloom is about what is left out — a single blossom dissolving into negative space, stillness between brushstrokes.

name: R. Mendez
bio: Street photographer turned silk artist. Wall Dragon began as a mural on a Shanghai back alley, photographed, then re-rendered for silk — urban art brought indoors.

name: H. Yamamoto
bio: Anime background artist and cel-shading specialist. Akira Requiem is a tribute to the cyberpunk frames that defined a generation of Japanese animation.

name: LYS Studio
bio: The in-house LYS studio. Works created or co-created by our own team — special projects, commemorative editions, and the 1/1 centrepieces of each season.
